subfamily: savory highball, served up (the Red Snapper)
glass: stemmed wine glass (about 250-300 ml), chilled, no ice
version: v1.3 (Tomás, round 5, 2026-10-01; drink unchanged from v1, notes corrected per Hester M1-M3): the Red Snapper as printed in Crosby Gaige's cocktail guide (1941, Hester F5–F6; Joy's copy is dated 1945, C1). Joy pdf 249: as much vodka as tomato juice, served straight up as a cocktail; Joy pdf 373, Regan's adapted recipe: 1.5 oz each, 2 dashes Worcestershire, 2 dashes lemon, salt and cayenne, shaken, strained, chilled cocktail glass. Vodka on the guide's own page (Hester F17, guide p. 57). Oxford BLOODY MARY pdf 293: in 1964 Petiot credited Jessel with the tomato juice-vodka combination; 'at the St. Regis, the drink was known as the Red Snapper'; pdf 292: a documented St. Regis speciality, 'spices and all', from at least 1941. Kept: equal parts vodka and tomato, and served up (Joy pdf 249); the shake is Regan's method (Joy pdf 373), my timing. Changed (mine, so never 'his recipe'): Worcestershire (gluten, safe side) and cayenne (spice) left off, veto-free; 15 ml manzanilla does the savoury work instead (Codex p. 221 suggests manzanilla in place of the vodka 'to up the savory ante'; ours is a splash beside it, the measure mine; Matrix pdf 245: sherry and vodka both on tomato's wheel); lemon raised from 2 dashes to 15 ml (Regan's proportions read flat at 0.22% acid); celery salt and salt. Freeform because Arnold has no savoury style: as shaken (10 s), 120 ml -> 45.2% dilution -> ~174 ml, 11.6% ABV, 0.92 g sugar/100 ml, 0.66% acid. References (my arithmetic): Regan's adapted recipe 13.2% / 1.0 g / 0.22%; the Codex's baseline Bloody Mary (p. 221, mix p. 295) ~11% / ~2 g / ~0.8% before melt (Worcestershire and hot-sauce acid uncounted). Tomato values unsourced; swept 2.5-4.0 g and 0.35-0.5%: 0.79-1.18 g, 0.65-0.69%. Vodka 37.5-50%: 11.1-13.8%. Wine glass, not Regan's cocktail glass: 174 ml finished overflows a standard cocktail glass. Guide's own recipe (Hester F17, guide p. 57, OCR of the 1946 fifth printing, copyright 1941): 2 oz tomato juice, 2 oz vodka, a fraction of a teaspoon of Worcestershire, a pinch of salt, rest cut off. Kept from it: equal parts and the pinch of salt; 45 ml each (not 2 oz) is mine, to keep it short. Gin version is a legend (L3).
